claims: Claim 0 forward (reverse=false, input_integers=output_integers=true, objective=Equal, inverse=1): every source-MI point maps to a complete target-MI point preserving all 11,717 coordinates and the objective; 64,544 obligations.

Claim 1 reverse integer (reverse=true, both integer flags true, inverse=0): every target-MI point maps back to a source-MI point; each of the 11,717 source declarations is discharged as VarInt or as one of the 4,502 locally proved unit-pivot Int facts; 69,046 obligations.

Claim 2 reverse continuous (reverse=true, both integer flags false, objective=Equal, no inverse): complete target-LP inclusion into the source LP in all coordinates with no integrality borrowed; 45,612 obligations.
The separately supplied cases/test26/request.json must equal the certificate claims exactly; it is the entire contract (1,550,763 B, three claims, no improvement, point or bijection claims).
proof_encoding: One RPA 2 certificate: 4,616 steps in 3 blocks - block 0 = 38 Cases (forward gate splits), block 1 = 4,540 Lin (4,502 Int pivot facts plus 38 reverse gate scalings), block 2 = 38 Lin (continuous reverse gate scalings); each block ends in Return{map of 11,717 Exprs, checks}.

179,202 positional check witnesses plus three 11,717-entry maps: proof.rpa 5,137,369 B -> proof.rpx 3,386,485 B; verify reports 179,202 obligations, 38 branches, 2,573,631 work, peak live facts 4,540, zero flow/interval/menu/signed lifts.

Reverse gate step is one Lin Le: scale the target row by the unit k and add the gate lower bound, checks.append(p.lin('Le',[[r,k],[{'VarLower':y},aa-k*q]],wanted)) - no Cases needed (tools/prepare_test26.py:45-46).

Forward gate step is a local Cases on the gate: gate = 0 branch is one Lin Le with the assumption; gate = 1 branch is EqPair(VarUpper,assumption) + Lin Le + Lin Int(sum) + Round + Lin Le composition (tools/prepare_test26.py:49-56 via tools/prepare_test44.py:11).

Obligation order is kernel-owned, generated from the output model: per output variable lower then upper Le plus Int when requested, then one Eq/Le per output row by sense, then the objective Eq, then projection pairs, then inverse pairs (crates/core/src/verify.rs:440-473).

No variable, row, bound, RHS, objective term or nonzero added or deleted; the target's COLUMNS reorder (retained-integer block first) permutes 11,710 of 11,717 coordinates.

friction: A coefficient-level edit has no representation: Claim (crates/core/src/proof.rs:7-31, deny_unknown_fields; documented at docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:339) offers only reverse, integer flags, objective, projection, affine_projection, inverse, objective level and halfspace, so the 190-record diff lives only in untrusted audit.json and Python assertions.

Coordinate binding is by position, not name: because the target COLUMNS are reordered, the compiler hand-wrote 11,717 pairs three times (141,819 B compact per claim; only 7 fixed points) although the two models share every variable name.

Obligation witnesses are positional and kernel-derived, so the compiler mirrors an internal order by hand (per variable lower/upper/Int, per row, objective, projection, inverse); attacks that drop check 20000 fail only as 'obligation 20000'.

97 percent of the certificate is filler: 179,202 obligations from 4,616 steps, so the preparer writes repetition in Python (checks += ['Exact'] * 11,717) and copies the 4,502-step proof order straight out of the audit hints.

Both rules are hand-composed step by step with Python-side coefficient recomputation (aa, k, q at tools/prepare_test26.py:41) and Python-side expected-expression asserts; a wrong recomputation surfaces only as a kernel obligation mismatch.
